messages.subject: [statnet_help] Nonedgewise Shared Partners
messages.body_plain:
Hi Zachary-

It's perhaps clearest if you think of the first term (edgewise, 
dyadwise, non-edgewise) in the context of the base unit the distribution 
is summed on.  I.e.

ESP distribution: for each pair of actors who are directly linked, how 
many shared partners do they have?
DSP distribution: for each pair of actors --regardless of whether they 
are linked or not--how many shared partners do they have?
NSP distribution: for each pair of actors who are *not* directly linked, 
how many shared partners do they have?

Thus the NSP distribution must equal the DSP distribution minus the ESP 
distribution.

You might wonder why one would ever use this?  Its uses are indeed rare 
and less easily interpreted relative to the ESP distribution, but it can 
be interesting as a point of comparison to have either the DSP or NSP in 
a model as well.

Steve

messages.subject: [statnet_help] statnetWeb -- looking for all of your feedback
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] statnetWeb -- looking for all of your feedback
messages.body_plain:
Dear statnet users,

The statnet team has been working on a web application to serve as a GUI for some of the
functionality?of the statnet packages. We envision that this web app - called statnetWeb -
will be an accessible?introduction to statnet for researchers without experience working in R
and a useful tool for teaching?statistical network analysis.

statnetWeb is written in R-Shiny (http://shiny.rstudio.com/) and the code is hosted on GitHub
(https://github.com/statnet/statnetWeb). We currently incorporate functionality from the
network, sna?and ergm packages so that users can upload network data, look at network plots
and summary statistics,?fit an ergm, assess the fit and simulate from the model.

The app is still in a prototype stage, but it's at a point where we would like feedback from
the community of existing statnet users.

You can run statnetWeb in two ways:
 ?*? Through the shinyapps server, by clicking this link:?https://ebey.shinyapps.io/statnetWeb/
 ?*? On your own machine through RStudio
 ? ? ?+? > install.packages(c("shiny", "shinyBS", "RColorBrewer", "statnet", "lattice",
"latticeExtra"))
 ? ? ?+? > library(shiny)
 ? ? ?+? > runGitHub("statnetWeb", "statnet")


Comments, questions, complaints and suggestions are all welcome. You can submit these through
the?Issues link on our GitHub page (https://github.com/statnet/statnetWeb) or via email.

Best,
Emily Beylerian and Martina Morris
for the statnet development team

messages.subject: [statnet_help] STERGM and bipartite networks
messages.body_plain:
Hi all -

The issue seems to be that both networksis and tergm contain a function 
named simulate.network.  This is an unfortunate choice on our part.  
We'll be revisiting the packages sometime soon, and we will decide on 
the best path forward.  In the meanwhile, a workaround is to use 
namespace notation to call the function you want, like so:

tergm:::simulate.network
networksis:::simulate.network

Note that because of R's dispatching rules, if you make a call to 
simulate with a network object as the first argument, it will then 
dispatch to simulate.network.  So if you need control over which version 
of simulate.network is being invoked there, don't call simulate; call 
simulate.network directly, with the above package name and triple colon.

I hope that helps,
Steve

messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

A couple weeks back there was some discussion on the list about how to 
interpret gw term components.  I mentioned I had a worksheet that I'd used 
to get some intuition about the function of the decay parameter (called 
"decay" for gwdegree and "alpha" for gw*sp), and some of you indicated an 
interest in seeing it.

So I've placed it up on the statnet wiki, on the Resources page:

https://statnet.csde.washington.edu/trac/attachment/wiki/Resources/GWDegree.xlsx

It works through how the decay influences the change statistic for the 
gwdegree term.  The gw*sp terms have similar responses to their decay 
parameter, but are a bit harder to explore in a simple sheet like this.

best,
Martina

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Simulating for ERGMs
messages.body_plain:
Dear StatNet Listserv,

As both an exercise for my students, and for my own education, I?ve been conducting some Monte Carlo experiments/simulations on the ERGM in order to ascertain how robust inferences from the ERGM are to a variety of simple specification and measurement issues. For example, one example might be trying to discover how severe coefficient biases are in the face of mounting data missingness. Such a simulation exercise requires that 1) I be able to replicate the data-generating process implied by ERGMs to create a network in which I know the relevant relationships perfectly, 2) be able to create some set of problems in said network, and then 3) estimate coefficients from an ERGM both on a true network and a network with some sort of problem to gauge the difference between those estimates.

Thus far, I have been using the ?simulate.ergm? command from statnet to create networks in which I can control coefficients perfectly. The simulate.ergm help file suggests that the command is used to ?draw from exponential family random network models,? and allows a user to set coefficient values using a ?coef? vector. So if I create a network with high levels of reciprocity using the simulate command by setting the ?mutual? coefficient for simulate to a value of 2, and then run an ERGM on the created network with a mutual term as a covariate, the coefficient on the mutual term should return a value of 2 (in expectation).

What I and my team are finding is that when networks are small (25 actors) this process works exactly as we thought, but as the network size increases (to say 75 or 100 actors), the simulate command no longer produces networks whose ERGM coefficients match what we think they should. In the above example, if we use simulate to create a network and set the mutual coefficient to 2 in the simulate command, then run an ERGM on that network, the estimated ERGM will report a mutual coefficient of 2 when the network is small, but as the network size increases, the estimated ERGM will report increasingly small coefficients even before we?ve introduced any sort of problems.

Since our ability to control the data generating process of the ERGM is central to our statistical experiments, we were hoping someone might be able to shed light on why the simulate.ergm command isn?t consistently producing networks in which the ERGM coefficients are what we would expect, particularly as our network sizes get larger. Below I?ve posted some sample R-code for how we?ve been running things along with some heavy commenting to illustrate what we?re trying to do, and I?m happy to chat off list if that?s easier for folks. Thanks in advance for any help anyone can provide.

-----------------------------------------------------------
EXAMPLE CODE:

#Clear Memory
rm(list=ls())

#load libraries
library(statnet)

#set seed
set.seed(1234)

#set parameters
initial.density<-0.2

#This sets the actor size of the network; increase this number and bad things happen
actors<-50

#Number of simulations
sims<-100

#These are our model parameters that we hope ERGM will recover; as our sample size gets larger, the ERGM coefficients are further
#and further from these parameters, even across thousands of simulations
update.density<-0.1
update.mutual<-2

#Create a place to store things
TrueCoefsE<-numeric(sims) #Store edges coefficients
TrueCoefsM<-numeric(sims) #Store mutual coefficients

for(k in 1:sims){

  #Draw a blank matrix
  Net<-matrix(0, actors, actors)

  #Fill in a blank adjacency matrix using the initial density parameter; this is largely just a set up to the actual network development
  for(i in 1:nrow(Net)){
    for(j in 1:nrow(Net)){
      Net[i,j]<-rbinom(1,1,initial.density)
    }
  }
  diag(Net)<-0

  #Turn into network object
  Net2<-network(Net, directed=TRUE)

  #Simulate intial ergm to get manipulable object; we?re going to use this model to control the DGP of the ERGM (hopefully)
  summary(mod.ini<-ergm(Net2~edges+mutual, control=control.ergm(MCMC.samplesize=5000, MCMLE.maxit=100, MCMC.burnin=10000, MCMC.interval=1000, drop=TRUE)))

  #Alter to coefficients to make into values you control; this is where we specify exactly what we want the coefficients from the ERGM to be
  coefs.ini<-coef(mod.ini)
  coefs.new<-coefs.ini
  coefs.new[1]<-update.density
  coefs.new[2]<-update.mutual

  #simulate new network with known coefficients; this SHOULD create a network in which the ERGM would report a mutual coefficient of 2/
  sim.new<-network(simulate(mod.ini, coef=coefs.new))

  #estimate ergm on new network with known coefficients
  summary(mod.new<-ergm(sim.new~edges+mutual, control=control.ergm(MCMC.samplesize=5000, MCMLE.maxit=100, MCMC.burnin=10000, MCMC.interval=1000, drop=TRUE)))

  #Store Coefficients
  TrueCoefsE[k]<-coef(mod.new)[1]
  TrueCoefsM[k]<-coef(mod.new)[2]
  print(k) #for tracking
}


#Plot the results
plot(density(TrueCoefsM), lwd=3, col="red", xlim=c(0, 3.5), ylim=c(0, 4), main="Distribution of Mutual Coefficients from ERGM")
abline(v=2, lwd=3, lty=2, col="black")
grid()
legend("topleft", c("Estimated Coefficients", "Truth"), lwd=c(3,3), lty=c(1,2), col=c("red", "black"))


End of Code
--------------------------------------------------------------------------


In the above code, we simulate a network with a clearly defined reciprocity coefficient, and then run an ERGM on that network that ought to return the coefficient value of 2 (or some number close to 2). We can increase the network?s size by changing the ?actors? parameter. As the number of actors in the network increases, the difference between the distribution of coefficients and the "truth? grows, even though absolutely nothing else about the simulation is changing. We don?t understand why this is happening. I?m sure I?m missing something self-evident, but I?ve been wracking my brain about why the ERGMs coefficients would decline as the networks size grows, though nothing else in the network DGP is changing. Any clarity would be really helpful.


Thanks in advance. Best,
Justin

Justin H. Kirkland
Assistant Professor
Department of Political Science
University of Houston
www.jhkirkla.wordpress.com<http://www.jhkirkla.wordpress.com>

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Simulating for ERGMs
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Justin -

Have you tried ensuring that your burn-in and thinning intervals are 
both substantially larger than N^2 (where N is the number of vertices)?  
The intervals you include below may prove insufficient once N approaches 
100 or so (though this depends).  Without having the chance to check 
over your code in detail, this immediately occurs to me as one factor 
that can lead to the effect you describe.  (FWIW, I recently did a 
simulation study using MCMC on the edge/mutual model for a different 
purpose, and I found that I needed about N^3 iterations to guarantee 
high quality draws.  For an N of 100, that means you ought be looking at 
about a million iterations, if you want to be extra safe.)  Try running 
the MCMC longer, and see if that works.

Hope that helps,

-Carter

messages.body_plain:
>From Li Wang:

Carter is right about the burn-in not being enough. Simply upping the
MCMC.burnin of simulate to 100000 solves the problem.

But, it's also worth noting the relationship between network density and 
the edge coefficient. By using an edge coefficient of 0.1, you are trying 
to simulate networks that are over 50% full from the edges term alone, and 
around 80% full after adding the mutual coef of 2. The initial network 
you use has density of 0.2; that's why such a long burn-in is necessary 
(to get to density 0.8).  So, this suggests other changes.

I've simplified and recoded your example to target a network with
density 0.1 (edge coef = -2.197) instead. The estimates match the true
value well.


#load libraries
library(statnet)

#set seed
set.seed(1234)

#set parameters
initial.density<-0.2

#This sets the actor size of the network
actors<-50

#Number of simulations
sims<-100

#These are our model parameters that we hope ERGM will recover; a
# note that the first one is a density, not an ERGM coefficient
update.density<-0.1
update.mutual<-2

#Create a place to store things
TrueCoefsE<-numeric(sims) #Store edges coefficients
TrueCoefsM<-numeric(sims) #Store mutual coefficients

for(k in 1:sims){
   #Initialize network with the right density
   Net <- network.initialize(actors, directed=T)
   Net <- san(Net ~ edges, target.stats=(actors^2-actors)*initial.density)

   # the edge coefficient is logit of density, if there are no other
terms involved
   edge.coef <- log(update.density/(1-update.density))
   coefs.new<-c(edge.coef, update.mutual)

   #simulate new network with known coefficients; this SHOULD create a
network in which the ERGM would report a mutual coefficient of 2/
   sim.new<-simulate(Net~edges+mutual, coef=coefs.new,
control=control.simulate(MCMC.burnin=100000))

   #estimate ergm on new network with known coefficients
   summary(mod.new<-ergm(sim.new~edges+mutual,
control=control.ergm(MCMC.samplesize=2^11, MCMLE.maxit=100,
MCMC.burnin=50000, MCMC.interval=2^11, drop=TRUE)))

   #Store Coefficients
   TrueCoefsE[k]<-coef(mod.new)[1]
   TrueCoefsM[k]<-coef(mod.new)[2]
   print(k) #for tracking
}

#Plot the results
plot(density(TrueCoefsM), lwd=3, col="red", xlim=c(0, 3.5), ylim=c(0,
4), main="Distribution of Mutual Coefficients from ERGM")
abline(v=2, lwd=3, lty=2, col="black")
grid()
legend("topleft", c("Estimated Coefficients", "Truth"), lwd=c(3,3),
lty=c(1,2), col=c("red", "black"))

> problems.

> central to our statistical experiments, we were hoping someone might be able
> to shed light on why the simulate.ergm command isn???t consistently
> producing networks in which the ERGM coefficients are what we would expect,
> particularly as our network sizes get larger. Below I???ve posted some

>     }
>   }
>   diag(Net)<-0
>
>   #Turn into network object
>   Net2<-network(Net, directed=TRUE)
>
>   #Simulate intial ergm to get manipulable object; we???re going to use this
> model to control the DGP of the ERGM (hopefully)
>   summary(mod.ini<-ergm(Net2~edges+mutual,
> control=control.ergm(MCMC.samplesize=5000, MCMLE.maxit=100,
> MCMC.burnin=10000, MCMC.interval=1000, drop=TRUE)))
>
>   #Alter to coefficients to make into values you control; this is where we
> specify exactly what we want the coefficients from the ERGM to be
>   coefs.ini<-coef(mod.ini)
>   coefs.new<-coefs.ini
>   coefs.new[1]<-update.density
>   coefs.new[2]<-update.mutual
>
>   #simulate new network with known coefficients; this SHOULD create a
> network in which the ERGM would report a mutual coefficient of 2/
>   sim.new<-network(simulate(mod.ini, coef=coefs.new))
>
>   #estimate ergm on new network with known coefficients
>   summary(mod.new<-ergm(sim.new~edges+mutual,
> control=control.ergm(MCMC.samplesize=5000, MCMLE.maxit=100,
> MCMC.burnin=10000, MCMC.interval=1000, drop=TRUE)))
>
>   #Store Coefficients
>   TrueCoefsE[k]<-coef(mod.new)[1]
>   TrueCoefsM[k]<-coef(mod.new)[2]
>   print(k) #for tracking
> }
>
>
> #Plot the results
> plot(density(TrueCoefsM), lwd=3, col="red", xlim=c(0, 3.5), ylim=c(0, 4),
> main="Distribution of Mutual Coefficients from ERGM")
> abline(v=2, lwd=3, lty=2, col="black")
> grid()
> legend("topleft", c("Estimated Coefficients", "Truth"), lwd=c(3,3),
> lty=c(1,2), col=c("red", "black"))
>
>
> End of Code
> --------------------------------------------------------------------------
>
>
> In the above code, we simulate a network with a clearly defined reciprocity
> coefficient, and then run an ERGM on that network that ought to return the
> coefficient value of 2 (or some number close to 2). We can increase the
> network???s size by changing the ???actors??  parameter. As the number of
> actors in the network increases, the difference between the distribution of
> coefficients and the "truth??  grows, even though absolutely nothing else
> about the simulation is changing. We don???t understand why this is
> happening. I???m sure I???m missing something self-evident, but I???ve been
> wracking my brain about why the ERGMs coefficients would decline as the
> networks size grows, though nothing else in the network DGP is changing. Any

messages.subject: [statnet_help] missing value in statnet
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Ya -

There is no uniform default way of handling missing data in networks - 
the applicable methods are necessarily technique and situation 
specific.  In the context of the ergm() function per se, the default is 
to use the latent missing data approach of Gile and Handcock; this 
marginalizes across the possible values of the missing edge variables, 
under the assumption that they and the observed edge variables were 
drawn from the same model (and that the pattern of missingness is 
ignorable).  Performing simulation from a model fit using this strategy, 
conditional on the observed data, can be used as a multiple imputation 
technique (e.g., for subsequent exploratory data analysis) and/or to get 
a sense of how well the model and observed data constrain the edge 
variables that were not observed.

Hope that helps,

-Carter
